1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
8	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
9	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
10	
11	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
12	
13	    query       := SELECT select_item (',' select_item)*
14	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
15	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
16	                   [LIMIT uint]
17	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')'
18	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')')
19	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
20	    expr       := or_expr
21	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
22	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
23	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
24	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
25	    postfix     := atom (IS [NOT] NULL)?
26	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
27	    operand     := ident | literal
28	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
29	                   | single-quoted utf8
30	
31	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
32	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Without
33	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
34	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
35	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
36	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported.
37	
38	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
39	NULL is a postfix of its atom.  Comparison operands must be column
40	references or literals.  WHERE follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
41	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
42	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
43	
44	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
45	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
46	of their first selected row.  ORDER BY may only name selected grouped
47	columns or selected aggregate expressions; ASC is the default, NULLs sort
48	last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST is given, and
49	groups equal on every sort key keep that first-row order.  LIMIT then
50	keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY and aggregates an aggregate
51	query over zero selected rows still yields one output row (COUNT 0, the
52	other aggregates NULL); with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
53	
54	Two-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add one equi-join to the grammar::
55	
56	    query := SELECT ... FROM left_table [join_kind JOIN right_table
57	             ON left_table.column = right_table.column] ...
58	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT
59	
60	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
61	the statement are read.  Aliases, compound ON conditions, other join types
62	and a second join are rejected as syntax errors before any file is opened.
63	In a join query every column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be
64	qualified as ``table.column`` (either part may be a double-quoted
65	identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the left schema followed by the right
66	schema with ``table.column`` names; explicit projections keep their
67	qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase ``FUNC(table.column)``
68	labels.  Join keys may share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys
69	never match.  INNER JOIN emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also
70	emits unmatched left rows with the right-side values set to NULL (the
71	right result columns are nullable).  Rows expand in left-file order, and
72	within one left row in right-file order, before WHERE / GROUP BY /
73	ORDER BY / LIMIT apply with their usual semantics.
74	"""

143	@dataclass(frozen=True)
144	class _Token:
145	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof

150	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
151	    r"""
152	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
153	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
154	    """,
155	    re.VERBOSE,

158	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)

161	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
162	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
163	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
164	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
165	    i = 0
166	    n = len(sql)
167	    while i < n:
168	        ch = sql[i]
169	        if ch.isspace():
170	            i += 1
171	            continue
172	        if ch == "*":
173	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
174	            i += 1
175	            continue
176	        if ch in ",()+-":
177	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
178	            i += 1
179	            continue
180	        if ch in "=<>!":
181	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
182	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
183	                i += 2
184	                continue
185	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
186	                op = ch + "="
187	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
188	                i += 2
189	                continue
190	            if ch in "=<>":
191	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
192	                i += 1
193	                continue
194	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
195	        if ch == "'":
196	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
197	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
198	            i = new_i
199	            continue
200	        if ch == '"':
201	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
202	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
203	            i = new_i
204	            continue
205	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
206	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
207	            if match:
208	                text = match.group(0)
209	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
210	                i = match.end()
211	                continue
212	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
213	            # used by two-table queries ("table.column").
214	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
215	            i += 1
216	            continue
217	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
218	        if match:
219	            text = match.group(0)
220	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
221	            i = match.end()
222	            continue
223	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
224	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
225	    return tokens

228	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
229	    lowered = word.lower()
230	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:

233	        if lowered == "false":
234	            return _Token("number", False, word)

236	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)

239	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
240	    parts: list[str] = []
241	    i = start + 1
242	    n = len(sql)
243	    while True:
244	        j = sql.find("'", i)
245	        if j == -1:
246	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
247	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
248	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
249	            parts.append("'")
250	            i = j + 2
251	            continue
252	        value = "".join(parts)
253	        try:
254	            value.encode("utf-8")
255	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
256	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
257	        return value, j + 1

260	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
261	    parts: list[str] = []
262	    i = start + 1
263	    n = len(sql)
264	    while True:
265	        j = sql.find('"', i)
266	        if j == -1:
267	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
268	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
269	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
270	            parts.append('"')
271	            i = j + 2
272	            continue
273	        value = "".join(parts)
274	        if not value:
275	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
276	        return value, j + 1

279	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
280	    try:
281	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
282	            value: int | float = float(text)
283	        else:
284	            value = int(text, 10)
285	    except ValueError:
286	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
287	    if isinstance(value, int):
288	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
289	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
290	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
291	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
292	        return value
293	    if not math.isfinite(value):
294	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
295	    return value

299	# Parsed expression tree

301	# Node tuples:
302	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
303	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
304	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
305	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
306	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)

309	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time).
310	#
311	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
312	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
313	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
314	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

321	    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg"
322	    name: str | None = None  # column name for kind == "column"
323	    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
324	    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
325	    descending: bool = False
326	    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
327	    # Table qualifiers (two-table queries only; None when unqualified):
328	    table: str | None = None
329	    table_quoted: bool = False
330	    arg_table: str | None = None
331	    arg_table_quoted: bool = False

334	@dataclass(frozen=True)
335	class _Join:
336	    """The single optional equi-join of a two-table query."""
337	
338	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left"
339	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
340	    table_quoted: bool
341	    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
342	    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)

345	@dataclass
346	class _Select:
347	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
348	    table: str
349	    table_quoted: bool
350	    where: tuple | None
351	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
352	    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
353	    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
354	    limit: int | None
355	    join: _Join | None = None
356	
357	    @property
358	    def star(self) -> bool:
359	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
360	
361	    @property
362	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
363	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
364	
365	    @property
366	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
367	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None

369	
370	class _Parser:
371	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
372	
373	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
374	        self.tokens = tokens
375	        self.pos = 0
376	        # Two-table statements (qualified names + one JOIN clause) are only
377	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
378	        # them as syntax errors.
379	        self._allow_join = allow_join
380	
381	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
382	        select = self._parse_select()
383	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
384	            tok = self._peek()
385	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
386	        return select
387	
388	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
389	        self._expect_keyword("select")
390	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
391	        self._expect_keyword("from")
392	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
393	        join = None
394	        if self._allow_join:
395	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
396	                self._expect_keyword("join")
397	                join = self._parse_join("inner")
398	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
399	                self._expect_keyword("join")
400	                join = self._parse_join("left")
401	        where = None
402	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
403	            where = self._parse_or()
404	        group_by = None
405	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
406	            self._expect_keyword("by")
407	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
408	            while self._accept_op(","):
409	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
410	            group_by = tuple(names)
411	        order_by = None
412	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
413	            self._expect_keyword("by")
414	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
415	            while self._accept_op(","):
416	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
417	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
418	        limit = None
419	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
420	            limit = self._parse_limit()
421	        return _Select(
422	            items=items,
423	            table=table_tok.value,
424	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
425	            where=where,
426	            group_by=group_by,
427	            order_by=order_by,
428	            limit=limit,
429	            join=join,
430	        )
431	
432	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
433	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
434	        self._expect_keyword("on")
435	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
436	        self._expect_op("=")
437	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
438	        return _Join(
439	            kind=kind,
440	            table=table_tok.value,
441	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
442	            left_key=left_key,
443	            right_key=right_key,
444	        )
445	
446	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
447	        tok = self._peek()
448	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
449	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
450	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
451	            )
452	        self._next()
453	        if not self._accept_op("."):
454	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
455	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
456	            )
457	        nxt = self._peek()
458	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
459	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
460	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
461	            )
462	        self._next()
463	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
464	
465	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
466	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
467	        while self._accept_op(","):
468	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
469	        # Aliases are not supported; a trailing identifier (including the
470	        # spelling "as") where FROM is expected names one.  Plain queries keep
471	        # their historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries
472	        # treat the unsupported alias as a validation error.
473	        tok = self._peek()
474	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
475	            grouped_ahead = any(
476	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
477	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
478	            )
479	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
480	                raise QueryValidationError(
481	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
482	                )
483	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
484	        return items
485	
486	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
487	        tok = self._peek()
488	        if tok.kind == "star":
489	            self._next()
490	            return _RefItem("star")
491	        return self._parse_column_or_agg()
492	
493	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
494	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
495	        descending = False
496	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
497	            descending = False
498	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
499	            descending = True
500	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
501	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
502	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
503	                nulls_first = True
504	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
505	                nulls_first = False
506	            else:
507	                tok = self._peek()
508	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
509	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
510	                )
511	        return _RefItem(
512	            item.kind,
513	            name=item.name,
514	            func=item.func,
515	            arg=item.arg,
516	            descending=descending,
517	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
518	            table=item.table,
519	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
520	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
521	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
522	        )
523	
524	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
525	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
526	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
527	
528	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
529	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
530	        table_tok = self._next()
531	        self._expect_op(".")
532	        name_tok = self._peek()
533	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
534	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
535	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
536	            )
537	        self._next()
538	        return _RefItem(
539	            "column",
540	            name=name_tok.value,
541	            table=table_tok.value,
542	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
543	        )
544	
545	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
546	        tok = self._peek()
547	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
548	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
549	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
550	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
551	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
552	        # can only be a plain column reference.
553	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
554	            self._next()
555	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
556	        func = tok.value.lower()
557	        self._next()  # consume the function name
558	        if not self._accept_op("("):
559	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
560	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
561	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
562	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
563	        self._expect_op(")")
564	        return _RefItem(
565	            "agg",
566	            func=func.upper(),
567	            arg=arg,
568	            arg_table=arg_table,
569	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
570	        )
571	
572	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
573	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
574	        # table-qualified) identifier.  Returns (name, table, table_quoted);
575	        # name "" stands for '*'.
576	        tok = self._peek()
577	        if tok.kind == "star":
578	            if func != "count":
579	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
580	            self._next()
581	            return ("", None, False)
582	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
583	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
584	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
585	            )
586	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
587	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
588	            nxt = self._peek()
589	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
590	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
591	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
592	                )
593	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
594	        self._next()
595	        nxt = self._peek()
596	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
597	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
598	                raise QueryValidationError(
599	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
600	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
601	                )
602	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
603	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
604	            )
605	        return (tok.value, None, False)
606	
607	    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
608	        tok = self._peek()
609	        if (
610	            tok.kind != "number"
611	            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
612	            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
613	        ):
614	            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
615	        self._next()
616	        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
617	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
618	                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
619	            )
620	        return tok.value
621	
622	    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
623	        tok = self._peek()
624	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
625	            return self._next()
626	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")
627	
628	    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
629	        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
630	        tok = self._peek()
631	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
632	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
633	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
634	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
635	            return (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
636	        self._next()
637	        return (None, False, tok.value)
638	
639	    # WHERE expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
640	
641	    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
642	        node = self._parse_and()
643	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
644	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
645	        return node
646	
647	    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
648	        node = self._parse_comparison()
649	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
650	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
651	        return node
652	
653	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
654	        left = self._parse_not_factor()
655	        tok = self._peek()
656	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
657	            self._next()
658	            right = self._parse_not_factor()
659	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
660	        return left
661	
662	    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
663	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
664	            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
665	        return self._parse_postfix()
666	
667	    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
668	        node = self._parse_atom()
669	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
670	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
671	            self._expect_keyword("null")
672	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
673	        return node
674	
675	    def _parse_atom(self) -> tuple:
676	        if self._accept_op("("):
677	            node = self._parse_or()
678	            self._expect_op(")")
679	            return node
680	        return self._parse_operand()
681	
682	    def _parse_operand(self) -> tuple:
683	        sign = 1
684	        tok = self._peek()
685	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
686	            if tok.value == "-":
687	                sign = -1
688	            self._next()
689	            tok = self._peek()
690	            if tok.kind != "number" or isinstance(tok.value, bool):
691	                raise QuerySyntaxError("sign must be followed by a numeric literal")
692	        if tok.kind == "number":
693	            self._next()
694	            value = tok.value
695	            if isinstance(value, bool):
696	                if sign == -1:
697	                    raise QuerySyntaxError("boolean literal cannot be negated")
698	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
699	            if isinstance(value, int):
700	                value *= sign
701	                if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
702	                    raise QuerySyntaxError("integer literal is outside the int64 range")
703	            else:
704	                value = math.copysign(value, sign) if sign == -1 else value
705	                if not math.isfinite(value):
706	                    raise QuerySyntaxError("float literal must be finite")
707	            type_name = "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64"
708	            return ("literal", value, type_name)
709	        if tok.kind == "string":
710	            if sign == -1:
711	                raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal cannot be negated")
712	            self._next()
713	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
714	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
715	            if sign == -1:
716	                raise QuerySyntaxError("column reference cannot be negated")
717	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
718	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
719	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
720	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
721	            if (
722	                tok.kind == "ident"
723	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
724	                and nxt.kind == "op"
725	                and nxt.value == "("
726	            ):
727	                raise QueryValidationError(
728	                    f"aggregate {tok.value.upper()}(...) is not allowed in WHERE"
729	                )
730	            self._next()
731	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
732	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
733	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in expression")
734	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in expression")
735	
736	    # Token helpers -----------------------------------------------------------
737	
738	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
739	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
740	
741	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
742	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
743	        self.pos += 1
744	        return tok
745	
746	    def _accept(self, kind: str) -> bool:
747	        if self._peek().kind == kind:
748	            self.pos += 1
749	            return True
750	        return False
751	
752	    def _accept_op(self, value: str) -> bool:
753	        tok = self._peek()
754	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
755	            self.pos += 1
756	            return True
757	        return False
758	
759	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
760	        tok = self._peek()
761	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:
762	            self.pos += 1
763	            return True
764	        return False
765	
766	    def _expect_keyword(self, value: str) -> _Token:
767	        tok = self._peek()
768	        if tok.kind != "keyword" or tok.value != value:
769	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")
770	        return self._next()
771	
772	    def _expect_op(self, value: str) -> _Token:
773	        tok = self._peek()
774	        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:
775	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value!r}, got {tok.text!r}")
776	        return self._next()

784	@dataclass(frozen=True)
785	class _BoundItem:
786	    """A validated projection element."""
787	
788	    kind: str  # "column" | "agg"
789	    output_name: str
790	    # kind == "column":
791	    col_index: int = -1
792	    # kind == "agg":
793	    func: str = ""
794	    arg_index: int = -1  # -1 means COUNT(*)
795	    arg_type: str = ""
796	    out_type: str = ""

800	def _bind_select(select: _Select, schema: Schema, expected_table="input") -> dict:
801	    if expected_table is not None:
802	        table_matches = (
803	            select.table == expected_table
804	            if select.table_quoted
805	            else select.table.lower() == expected_table.lower()
806	        )
807	        if not table_matches:
808	            raise QueryValidationError(
809	                f"unknown table {select.table!r}; only {expected_table!r} is supported"
810	            )
811	
812	    where = _bind_expr(select.where, schema) if select.where is not None else None
813	    if where is not None and where[0] in ("literal", "column"):
814	        type_name = _operand_type(where)
815	        if type_name != "bool":
816	            raise QueryValidationError(
817	                f"WHERE clause must be boolean, got {type_name}"
818	            )
819	
820	    if not select.is_aggregate_query:
821	        return _bind_plain(select, schema, where)
822	    return _bind_aggregate(select, schema, where)
823	
824	
825	def _bind_plain(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
826	    # Non-aggregate path: '*' or a comma-separated list of plain columns.
827	    if select.star:
828	        indices = tuple(range(len(schema.columns)))
829	    else:
830	        seen: set[str] = set()
831	        indices_list: list[int] = []
832	        for item in select.items:
833	            if item.kind == "star":
834	                # A star mixed into a plain projection remains grammatical.
835	                raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' cannot be mixed with other projection items")
836	            name = item.name
837	            if name in seen:
838	                raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate column in projection: {name!r}")
839	            seen.add(name)
840	            try:
841	                indices_list.append(schema.index(name))
842	            except KeyError:
843	                raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
844	        indices = tuple(indices_list)
845	    order_by = _bind_plain_order_by(select.order_by, schema)
846	    return {
847	        "mode": "plain",
848	        "indices": indices,
849	        "where": where,
850	        "order_by": order_by,
851	    }
852	
853	
854	def _bind_plain_order_by(select_order_by, schema: Schema):
855	    if select_order_by is None:
856	        return None
857	    bound: list[tuple[int, bool, bool]] = []
858	    order_seen: set[str] = set()
859	    for item in select_order_by:
860	        if item.kind == "agg":
861	            raise QueryValidationError(
862	                f"aggregate {item.func}({_arg_label(item)}) may appear in ORDER BY "
863	                "only as part of an aggregate query"
864	            )
865	        name = item.name
866	        if name in order_seen:
867	            raise QueryValidationError(
868	                f"duplicate column in ORDER BY: {name!r}"
869	            )
870	        order_seen.add(name)
871	        try:
872	            col_index = schema.index(name)
873	        except KeyError:
874	            raise QueryValidationError(
875	                f"unknown ORDER BY column: {name!r}"
876	            ) from None
877	        nulls_first = item.nulls_first if item.nulls_first is not None else False
878	        bound.append((col_index, item.descending, nulls_first))
879	    return tuple(bound)

881	
882	def _bind_aggregate(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
883	    if select.star:
884	        raise QueryValidationError("'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY")
885	
886	    # Resolve GROUP BY columns first: order matters for the grouping key, and
887	    # duplicates / unknown columns are rejected here.  Entries are
888	    # (table, table_quoted, name) triples; names reaching the binder are
889	    # already canonical (single-file queries never carry a qualifier).
890	    group_indices: list[int] = []
891	    group_seen: set[str] = set()
892	    for _table, _table_quoted, name in select.group_by or ():
893	        if name in group_seen:
894	            raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate column in GROUP BY: {name!r}")
895	        group_seen.add(name)
896	        try:
897	            group_indices.append(schema.index(name))
898	        except KeyError:
899	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown GROUP BY column: {name!r}") from None
900	    group_index_set = set(group_indices)
901	
902	    # Resolve the projection.  Plain columns must be grouped; output names
903	    # (group column names and canonical "FUNC(arg)" labels) must be unique.
904	    bound_items: list[_BoundItem] = []
905	    output_seen: set[str] = set()
906	    has_plain = False
907	    for item in select.items:
908	        if item.kind == "star":
909	            raise QueryValidationError(
910	                "'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY"
911	            )
912	        if item.kind == "column":
913	            has_plain = True
914	            name = item.name
915	            try:
916	                col_index = schema.index(name)
917	            except KeyError:
918	                raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
919	            if col_index not in group_index_set:
920	                raise QueryValidationError(
921	                    f"column {name!r} must appear in GROUP BY or be wrapped in an aggregate"
922	                )

1072	def _bind_expr(node: tuple, schema: Schema) -> tuple:
1073	    tag = node[0]
1074	    if tag == "literal":
1075	        return node
1076	    if tag == "column":
1077	        name = node[1]
1078	        try:
1079	            index = schema.index(name)
1080	        except KeyError:
1081	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1082	        col = schema.columns[index]
1083	        return ("column", name, index, col.type, col.nullable)
1084	    if tag == "not":
1085	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1086	        _require_boolean(operand, "NOT")
1087	        return ("not", operand)
1088	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1089	        left = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1090	        right = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
1091	        _require_boolean(left, tag.upper())
1092	        _require_boolean(right, tag.upper())
1093	        return (tag, left, right)
1094	    if tag == "isnull":
1095	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1096	        if operand[0] not in ("literal", "column"):
1097	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
1098	                "IS NULL operand must be a column reference or a literal"
1099	            )
1100	        return ("isnull", operand, node[2])
1101	    if tag == "cmp":
1102	        op = node[1]
1103	        left = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
1104	        right = _bind_expr(node[3], schema)
1105	        if left[0] not in ("literal", "column") or right[0] not in ("literal", "column"):
1106	            raise QuerySyntaxError("comparison operands must be column references or literals")
1107	        left_t = _operand_type(left)
1108	        right_t = _operand_type(right)
1109	        if "bool" in (left_t, right_t):
1110	            if left_t != "bool" or right_t != "bool":
1111	                raise QueryValidationError(
1112	                    f"bool can only be compared to bool, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1113	                )
1114	            if op not in ("=", "!="):
1115	                raise QueryValidationError(f"bool only supports = and !=, not {op!r}")
1116	        elif "utf8" in (left_t, right_t):
1117	            if left_t != "utf8" or right_t != "utf8":
1118	                raise QueryValidationError(
1119	                    f"utf8 can only be compared to utf8, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1120	                )
1121	        elif not {left_t, right_t} <= {"int64", "float64"}:

1123	                f"cannot compare values of type {left_t} and {right_t}"

1146	def _eval(node: tuple, row: tuple) -> bool | None:
1147	    tag = node[0]
1148	    if tag == "literal":
1149	        return node[1]
1150	    if tag == "column":
1151	        return row[node[2]]
1152	    if tag == "isnull":
1153	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1154	        result = value is None
1155	        return (not result) if node[2] else result
1156	    if tag == "not":
1157	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1158	        return None if value is None else (not value)
1159	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1160	        # Short-circuit SQL semantics; UNKNOWN propagates only when needed.
1161	        if tag == "and":
1162	            left = _eval(node[1], row)
1163	            if left is False:
1164	                return False
1165	            right = _eval(node[2], row)
1166	            if right is False:
1167	                return False
1168	            if left is None or right is None:
1169	                return None
1170	            return True
1171	        left = _eval(node[1], row)
1172	        if left is True:
1173	            return True
1174	        right = _eval(node[2], row)
1175	        if right is True:
1176	            return True
1177	        if left is None or right is None:
1178	            return None
1179	        return False
1180	    if tag == "cmp":
1181	        left = _eval(node[2], row)
1182	        right = _eval(node[3], row)
1183	        if left is None or right is None:
1184	            return None
1185	        op = node[1]
1186	        if op == "=":
1187	            result = left == right
1188	        elif op == "!=":
1189	            result = left != right
1190	        elif op == "<":
1191	            result = left < right
1192	        elif op == "<=":
1193	            result = left <= right
1194	        elif op == ">":
1195	            result = left > right
1196	        else:  # ">="
1197	            result = left >= right
1198	        return bool(result)
1199	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover

1207	def _aggregate_value(func: str, arg_index: int, arg_type: str, rows, source_columns):
1208	    if func == "COUNT":
1209	        if arg_index == -1:
1210	            return len(rows)
1211	        col = source_columns[arg_index]
1212	        return sum(1 for i in rows if col[i] is not None)
1213	
1214	    col = source_columns[arg_index]
1215	    values = [col[i] for i in rows if col[i] is not None]
1216	    if not values:
1217	        return None
1218	
1219	    if func == "MIN":
1220	        return min(values)
1221	    if func == "MAX":
1222	        return max(values)
1223	    if func == "SUM":
1224	        if arg_type == "int64":
1225	            # Python integers are unbounded; the int64 result is rejected only
1226	            # when the final total leaves the int64 range.
1227	            total = sum(values)
1228	            if not (_INT64_MIN <= total <= _INT64_MAX):
1229	                raise QueryValidationError("SUM overflowed the int64 range")
1230	            return total
1231	        try:
1232	            total = math.fsum(values)
1233	        except OverflowError:
1234	            raise QueryValidationError("SUM produced a non-finite float64 value") from None
1235	        if not math.isfinite(total):
1236	            raise QueryValidationError("SUM produced a non-finite float64 value")
1237	        return total
1238	    # AVG
1239	    try:
1240	        result = math.fsum(values) / len(values)
1241	    except OverflowError:
1242	        raise QueryValidationError("AVG produced a non-finite float64 value") from None
1243	    if not math.isfinite(result):
1244	        raise QueryValidationError("AVG produced a non-finite float64 value")
1245	    return result

1253	def query_file(path: Any, sql: str) -> Table:
1254	    """Run ``sql`` against the single columnar file ``path``.
1255	
1256	    Returns a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table` with columns in
1257	    projection order.  Rows are filtered by WHERE, then grouped (for
1258	    aggregate queries) or sorted by ORDER BY, then capped by LIMIT, then
1259	    projected; without ORDER BY the file's original row order (or the
1260	    first-selected-row group order) is kept.  The statement is parsed
1261	    before the file is touched, so purely grammatical errors surface as
1262	    :class:`QuerySyntaxError` regardless of whether ``path`` exists.
1263	    Unknown columns, duplicate result columns, the wrong table name,
1264	    type-incompatible predicates, ungrouped columns, illegal aggregate
1265	    arguments or int64 SUM overflow raise :class:`QueryValidationError`;
1266	    malformed files raise :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.ColumnarFormatError`;
1267	    other I/O failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
1268	    """
1269	    tokens = _tokenize(sql)
1270	    select = _Parser(tokens).parse()
1271	    table = read_file(path)
1272	    return _run_query(table, select)

1282	def query_files(sources: Any, sql: str) -> Table:
1283	    """Run ``sql`` against the tables named by ``sources``.
1284	
1285	    ``sources`` maps table names to columnar file paths; only the tables
1286	    referenced by the statement are read.  The statement may join two of
1287	    them once (``INNER JOIN`` / ``LEFT JOIN ... ON t1.col = t2.col``); see
1288	    the module docstring for the exact grammar and semantics.
1289	
1290	    A non-mapping or empty ``sources``, non-string keys or non-path values
1291	    raise :class:`ValueError` before any file is touched.  Lexical and
1292	    grammatical errors (including join-keyword, ON and multiple-join
1293	    problems) raise :class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is read.
1294	    Unknown tables or columns, unqualified column references in a join
1295	    query, duplicate tables, misattributed or type-incompatible join keys
1296	    and duplicate result columns raise :class:`QueryValidationError`;
1297	    malformed files raise :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.ColumnarFormatError`;
1298	    other I/O failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
1299	    """
1300	    paths = _validate_sources(sources)
1301	    tokens = _tokenize(sql)
1302	    select = _Parser(tokens, allow_join=True).parse()
1303	    left_key = _resolve_table_ref(select.table, select.table_quoted, tuple(paths))
1304	    if select.join is None:
1305	        rewritten = _rewrite_select(select, _single_table_resolver(left_key))
1306	        table = read_file(paths[left_key])
1307	        return _run_query(table, rewritten, expected_table=None)
1308	
1309	    join = select.join
1310	    right_key = _resolve_table_ref(join.table, join.table_quoted, tuple(paths))
1311	    if right_key == left_key:
1312	        raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate table {right_key!r} in join")
1313	    on_left = _resolve_table_ref(join.left_key[0], join.left_key[1], (left_key, right_key))
1314	    on_right = _resolve_table_ref(join.right_key[0], join.right_key[1], (left_key, right_key))
1315	    if on_left != left_key or on_right != right_key:
1316	        raise QueryValidationError(
1317	            "ON keys must reference the left and right tables respectively"
1318	        )
1319	    # Qualifier checks (unqualified / unknown-table column references) do
1320	    # not need the files and run before any read.
1321	    rewritten = _rewrite_select(select, _join_resolver(left_key, right_key))
1322	    left_table = read_file(paths[left_key])
1323	    right_table = read_file(paths[right_key])

1477	            col.type,
1478	            True if join.kind == "left" else col.nullable,
1479	        )
1480	        for col in right.schema.columns
1481	    ]
1482	    names = [col.name for col in combined_columns]
1483	    if len(set(names)) != len(names):
1484	        raise QueryValidationError("joined tables produce duplicate column names")
1485	    schema = Schema(combined_columns)

1490	def _join_columns(
1491	    left: Table, right: Table, left_idx: int, right_idx: int, kind: str
1492	) -> list:
1493	    """Nested-loop equi-join preserving left-then-right file row order."""
1494	    left_cols = left._columns
1495	    right_cols = right._columns

1497	    right_width = len(right_cols)
1498	    # NULL keys never match, so they stay out of the right-side index.
1499	    index: dict[Any, list[int]] = {}
1500	    for j, key in enumerate(right_cols[right_idx]):

1507	        if matches:

1509	                for c in range(left_width):

1521	def _run_query(table: Table, select: _Select, expected_table="input") -> Table:
1522	    bound = _bind_select(select, table.schema, expected_table)
1523	    source_columns = table._columns

1526

1531	            i
1532	            for i in range(row_count)

1542	    indices = bound["indices"]

1560	    group_indices = bound["group_indices"]
1561	    bound_items = bound["items"]
1562	    order_by = bound["order_by"]
1563	    source_columns = table._columns
1564

1566	        [
1567	            ColumnSchema(item.output_name, item.out_type, nullable=item.nullable)
1568	            for item in bound_items

1574	    else:

1609	    selected: list[int],
1610	    source_columns: tuple[tuple, ...],
1611	    group_indices: tuple[int, ...],
1612	) -> list[tuple[int, ...]]:

1628	    order_by: tuple[tuple[int, bool, bool], ...],
1629	):

1643	    rows: list[tuple],
1644	    order_by: tuple[tuple[int, bool, bool], ...],
